title: A Generalization of the Avellaneda–Stoikov Market Making Framework: A Hybrid Minimax Inventory Pressure Control Approach
content: This paper introduces a novel Inventory Pressure Control (IPC) framework for High-Frequency Trading (HFT) market making. Departing from traditional stochastic control models requiring continuous price-drift estimation, our approach combines control theory with microstructural technical analysis via a saturated parametric nonlinear feedback architecture. The model incorporates volatility, order flow imbalance, queue risk, and toxic flow indicators into a hybrid mechanism that couples passive limit-order provision with active market-order rebalancing. Under discrete-time, heavy-tailed stochastic compound processes, we establish the local asymptotic boundedness and stochastic stability of the closed-loop inventory dynamics. Within this stable operational domain, we apply the discrete-time Minimax Dynamic Programming (DP) principle and derive the associated Bellman equation to construct a robust control policy that optimizes profit-risk trade-offs against worst-case market scenarios. We prove the local profitability of the proposed strategy and illustrate its efficiency through a numerical computational example.
